wrong_answer_semantics: B asserts that two copies of the pictured U-shaped pentomino cannot be cut from the board. The independently saved exact enumeration has six disjoint pairs, including rotation-only witnesses, so B is false.
mechanism: Paired three-cell red and two-cell blue exterior spans compare the U-piece B with a quarter-turned 2 by 3 fit in the board. Predicted error: examine two U-pieces with their mouths kept in the displayed orientation, find unavoidable overlap, and declare B impossible without allowing a relative half-turn or a common quarter-turn. This tests orientation freedom of a concave U rather than C long-arm bounding boxes.

source_reference: Current user Plane233 C01, actually viewed; true open-L boundary lengths paired red/blue, no source partition. Migrated to detached span annotations to preserve the physical-paper interpretation.
material_difference_from_all_known_prior: No historical tested Plane218 design existed. The current p01 four-long/two-high C bounding-span hypothesis produced complete B,C finals against preset C and is permanently excluded. This proposal uses a different 3 by 2 concave U, red/blue axes exchanged through an explicit quarter-turn comparison and the relative orientation of its open mouths. It is not a recolor, width change or rerun of p01.
human_semantics_before_visual_review: Every added mark is outside the material with a nonzero gap and short perpendicular end caps: an external dimension/comparison bracket, not transported colored edging. Original grids, all unit-cell fills, all source/option boundaries and labels are untouched. The 4 independent brackets are open; no interior partition, closed region or third area-bearing piece is drawn. Under physical paper/ink reading all shown material remains exactly the original black-white material. Actual image still requires primary visual review before calls.
conciseness: Four meaningful span lines plus their eight extent caps. Each cap disambiguates a true endpoint; no overwritten or duplicate properties.
